newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal to apply for WTO membership.
newsitem.headline: Nepal to apply for WTO membership.

text.p: Nepal will apply to join the World Trade Organisation (WTO) to benefit from concessions available to its least developed member countries, officials said on Saturday.

"Unless you become a member you cannot benefit from facilities given under the WTO regime by other countries," Mohan Dev Pant, the highest ranking civil servant in the Commerce Ministry, told Reuters.

Currently Nepal has observer status at the Geneva-based WTO. Pant said the centre-right coalition government had decided to seek membership in WTO, and Nepal would now submit a memorandum on its trade policies to the organisation.
After WTO member nations have reviewed the memorandum, which can take as long as a year, Nepal will submit a formal application, Pant said.
Nepal set up a task force in 1995 to study the implications of joining the world trade body, including the impact such a move would have on trading arrangements with neighbouring India.
A bilateral trade treaty allows all Nepali goods except cigarettes, alcohol and cosmetics to enter the Indian market free of duty.
In return, the kingdom offers favourable import duties on Indian goods, which account for 29 percent of Nepal's foreign purchases.

"We have already checked that bilateral trade arrangements we already have before becoming a WTO member would not be affected," Pant said, adding that it was time for Nepal to join the WTO, whose members account for most global trade.
Nepal is not entitled to most favoured nation status (MFN) unless it joins the WTO, authorities said.
MFN is an undertaking by two countries to give each other the maximum tariff concessions on their mutual trade which they already grant to other countries.
Additional benefits are also given to least developed member countries, officials said.
